items.name: Jingle Bells
items.blurb: Jingle Bells, by James Lord Pierpont (1857).
lyrics: Jingle bells, jingle bells
Jingle all the way
Oh, what fun it is to ride
In a one-horse open sleigh

audio.credit: James Lord Pierpont (composer); transcribed by Clued from public-domain sources; Salamander Grand Piano samples by Alexander Holm (CC BY 3.0)

items.name: Silent Night
items.blurb: Silent Night, by Franz Xaver Gruber (1818).
lyrics: Silent night, holy night
All is calm, all is bright
Round yon virgin mother and child
Holy infant so tender and mild

audio.credit: Franz Xaver Gruber (composer); transcribed by Clued from public-domain sources; Salamander Grand Piano samples by Alexander Holm (CC BY 3.0)

items.name: Deck the Halls
items.blurb: A Welsh melody from the 1700s with English words from 1862.
lyrics: Deck the halls with boughs of holly
Fa la la la la, la la la la
'Tis the season to be jolly
Fa la la la la, la la la la

audio.credit: Traditional (composer); transcribed by Clued from public-domain sources; Salamander Grand Piano samples by Alexander Holm (CC BY 3.0)

items.name: We Wish You a Merry Christmas
items.blurb: We Wish You a Merry Christmas.
lyrics: We wish you a Merry Christmas
We wish you a Merry Christmas
We wish you a Merry Christmas
And a Happy New Year

audio.credit: Traditional (composer); transcribed by Clued from public-domain sources; Salamander Grand Piano samples by Alexander Holm (CC BY 3.0)

items.name: Joy to the World
items.blurb: Joy to the World, by Lowell Mason (tune "Antioch"), words by Isaac Watts (1839).
lyrics: Joy to the world, the Lord is come
Let earth receive her King

audio.credit: Lowell Mason (tune "Antioch"), words by Isaac Watts (composer); transcribed by Clued from public-domain sources; Salamander Grand Piano samples by Alexander Holm (CC BY 3.0)

items.name: Greensleeves
items.blurb: An English folk tune from the 1500s, later used for the carol "What Child Is This?".
lyrics: Alas, my love, you do me wrong
To cast me off discourteously

audio.credit: Traditional (composer); transcribed by Clued from public-domain sources; Salamander Grand Piano samples by Alexander Holm (CC BY 3.0)

items.name: Amazing Grace
items.blurb: Words by John Newton (1779), sung to the American tune "New Britain" (1835).
lyrics: Amazing grace, how sweet the sound
That saved a wretch like me
I once was lost, but now am found
Was blind, but now I see

audio.credit: Traditional American tune "New Britain"; words by John Newton (composer); transcribed by Clued from public-domain sources; Salamander Grand Piano samples by Alexander Holm (CC BY 3.0)

items.name: Oh! Susanna
lyrics: I come from Alabama with my banjo on my knee
I'm going to Louisiana, my true love for to see

audio.credit: Stephen Foster (composer); transcribed by Clued from public-domain sources; Salamander Grand Piano samples by Alexander Holm (CC BY 3.0)

items.name: Daisy Bell (Bicycle Built for Two)
items.blurb: Daisy Bell (Bicycle Built for Two), by Harry Dacre (1892).
lyrics: Daisy, Daisy, give me your answer, do
I'm half crazy all for the love of you

audio.credit: Harry Dacre (composer); transcribed by Clued from public-domain sources; Salamander Grand Piano samples by Alexander Holm (CC BY 3.0)

items.name: Take Me Out to the Ball Game
items.blurb: Take Me Out to the Ball Game, by Albert Von Tilzer (1908).
lyrics: Take me out to the ball game
Take me out with the crowd
Buy me some peanuts and Cracker Jack
I don't care if I never get back

audio.credit: Albert Von Tilzer (composer); transcribed by Clued from public-domain sources; Salamander Grand Piano samples by Alexander Holm (CC BY 3.0)
